added.name: Gutgutgoose
added.long_description:
Most data companies pay for their data. Ours pays for itself.
Customers send us a stool sample. We sequence it, build a metabolic model of that gut, and simulate whether each probiotic strain has an open niche it can colonize. We formulate the best candidates, then re-sequence 90 days later to see what actually took hold and what changed. Each cycle gives us the baseline gut, the intervention, and the outcome. At scale, the endgame is models that predict chronic disease years before symptoms.
added.one_liner: AI training infrastructure via custom probiotics

long_description.before:
Tilt lets anyone build evidence-backed, point-in-time, and deterministic rules-based investment strategies... in minutes. If you're thinking about working here, we're on a mission to price the world's information.
long_description.after:

We operate across two connected surfaces: InvestOS, an open standard that lets any brokerage or platform plug verified methodology into its own AI experience; and Tilt, the reference implementation of InvestOS. Tilt is an agentic harness where investors, portfolio managers, and creators can author, remix, and publish strategies. 

If you're thinking about working here, our mission is to price the world's information.

long_description.before:
We are building Vela, the AI scheduling assistant for the most complex interactions. Everyone assumes scheduling is a calendaring problem. It's not. It's a human nuance problem: knowing who to prioritize, how hard to push, and which dynamics to navigate. Vela understands these nuances, and every interaction deepens that understanding.

Instead of manually calling, texting, and emailing hundreds of candidates across spreadsheets, today teams connect their system of record to Vela and it handles outreach, scheduling, and confirmation automatically with the nuances of industries and teams built in.

Gobhanu and Saatvik are brothers who scaled a microfinance bank to 77 countries as kids. We previously built at AWS ML + SuperCompute and BCG AI.
long_description.after:
Scheduling one interview panel takes a dozen emails. Then someone moves a call and you start over. 

Vela is an AI Scheduling Coordinator that handles it end to end. Just CC Vela on the thread like you would a person. It reaches out, finds times that work for everyone, chases the people who don't reply, reschedules when things change, and confirms. Over email, SMS, and WhatsApp, at any hour your candidate happens to respond.

No dashboard. No new workflow. Your team works the way it already works, without the scheduling.

one_liner.before: AI Agents For Complex Scheduling Coordination
one_liner.after: AI Recruiting Coordinator for Executive Search

long_description.before: Bizmark is the bespoke operating system for manufacturers. It connects the systems, spreadsheets, and knowledge a company already has, and turns them into optimized decisions and automated workflows: quotes priced in minutes, schedules that reflow when a machine goes down, inventory balanced between service levels and cash. Working product in weeks, not years. Building it with our first customers now.
long_description.after:
Bizmark is the operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods.

Legacy ERPs force operators into templates that don’t reflect how the business runs. As a result, decisions that directly affect revenue, margins, and service levels are made from spreadsheets, with less information than the company has, often by whoever is closest, not whoever knows best.

Bizmark solves this by connecting to the systems, inboxes, spreadsheets, documents, and the knowledge that lives in people’s heads, then turning that context into optimized decisions and automated workflows. Bizmark adapts to how each company operates, not the other way around. And customers get a working product in weeks, not years.

Some of the most innovative American companies use Bizmark to transform their operations.

one_liner.before: The bespoke operating system for manufacturers.
one_liner.after: The OS for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods

long_description.before:
Definite builds AI agents that generate the reports banks and financial institutions file with their regulators. Before any number lands in a filing, our verification engine checks it independently. Every line gets recomputed from ledger records and checked against a versioned rulebook, and wrong outputs go back to the agent with the reason, like compiler errors. They don't ship.

We met our first year studying computer science at the University of Waterloo, and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo, places where one unverified number in a filing has real consequences. At BitGo, attestations proving customer assets matched the ledger were assembled by hand every period. At Optiver, daily regulatory numbers were rebuilt manually because nothing downstream took them on faith.

Today a controller pulls data from the core system into Excel and maps it to the report line by line. By the regulators' own estimate, one quarterly filing takes weeks. The software banks buy for this validates formatting, not truth: a loan mapped to the wrong schedule line passes every check it runs, and an executive personally signs the result.

This is hard because verification has to be independent of the model doing the work. Recomputing every number from source records is the only check a regulator or auditor will accept, and it's why DeepSeek v3 with our engine beats GPT-5 on public reporting benchmarks.

Every regulated institution files these reports, forever. Whoever proves the numbers owns the layer the filings, the audits, and eventually the books themselves depend on. We build it, and the agents that run on it.
long_description.after:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.

one_liner.before: The most accurate financial agents for reporting
one_liner.after: Build everyday back-office agents on one live model of your books
